verdicts.why: Reads the fanatical patriotism of the gloss as bellicose eagerness, a force claim inside the word, and the negative charge fits 'fanatically'.
Keeps to the love-of-country gloss and places the word against patriotic by manner rather than by who uses it; positive charge fits.
Picks up the 'impurity' clause of the gloss, the examples (diamond, complexion) fit this sense, and the positive charge is right.
Register contrast with complete plus the gloss's 'having all necessary qualities' turned into praise; examples fit and charge is positive.
Reads the word's form (kept whole, not achieved) and register against faultless without leaving the 'without fault or error' gloss.
Plain-statement reading of 'without a flaw' against the warmer flawless; a mild positive charge is still plausible for a no-flaw gloss.
Stays on the errors-or-alterations gloss, contrasts with flawed on force, and the 'corrupt text' example fits this sense.
Distinguishes the participle's backward look from corrupt without changing sense; example of a corrupted language fits the gloss.
Characterises the word's lightness against defective as a matter of attitude, not referent, so it stays on 'having a defect' with a negative charge.
Plain-word reading of 'not perfect' contrasted with defective on force; all three examples fit this sense and the charge is negative.
Restates 'not created for a particular occasion' as kept-ready and marks it neutral; 'standing committee' fits.
Holds to the use-of-the-mind gloss with a register contrast against mental and a neutral charge; example fits.
Register placement (abstract, academic, high style) against mental on the same gloss, neutral charge.
Reads both directions of 'affecting or influenced by' the mind and contrasts with psychogenic; examples fit this non-paranormal sense.
Resists the commoner 'sensible' sense and stays on the mind-as-agent gloss; the example fits and the neutral charge is right.
Mildness reading of 'fail to meet hopes or expectations' set against fail's abandonment; the Austen examples fit and the charge is negative.
Covers both halves of the gloss (prove undependable; abandon) and characterises the word's framing; 'courage did not fail her' fits.
'British' is a register label; the rest reads 'out of patience' in a casual key against exasperated, with a negative charge.
Keeps to the surfeit gloss rather than the commoner revulsion sense, and the example fits.
Reads 'experiencing or manifesting displeasure' as the cool baseline of the family, which makes the 0 neutral-in-family charge plausible.
Lightness and belittling of the feeling against annoyed, all inside the 'aroused to impatience or anger' gloss; negative charge fits.
Register reading (rude, blunt, crude) against displeased on the anger gloss; the example is the anger sense, not the drunk one.
Describes the word's texture (churning, unsettled) against stung on the same gloss; 'roiled by the delay' fits.
Sudden-recoil reading of the anger gloss set against irritated's wear; stays inside the word, negative charge.
Approval with respect matches 'inspiring admiration or approval', contrast with charming is on force; example fits, positive charge.
Stays on the 'capable of winning favor' gloss without importing the sycophantic sense, and the neutral charge fits a capability gloss.
Register label (informal, homely) plus a force contrast with attainable on the attainability gloss; example fits, positive charge.
Procedural reading of 'capable of being done with means at hand' with no judgment, matching the neutral charge.
